At the current state of the Early Access, I feel the game simply dumps too much on the player without giving the resources to handle it through skill. Rather it is mostly luck if you can succeed or not. At around 80% progress through the first level, I found it boils down to repairing the rail switch lever and the engine itself. There are simply too many enemies with not enough damage to deal with them so the only option left is to hope you live. I also feel shops are too rare. I often find myself dying with upwards of 700 scrap from the factory module and it leads to frustration as a shop rarely if ever appears to even use the scrap on. Overall, I feel the game just stacks way too many high hit point enemies on top of each other and if you only have the cannon due to horrid luck which seems more often than not, then there is no hope. Many enemies take over half of the cannon's magazine size to even kill so it's a futile effort to even try killing them to a certain point when more and more and more start showing up. The problem would be mediated if 80% of the upgrades weren't mostly useless or straight up didn't work like "sundering" or "burning" upgrades without the prerequisites of a source to apply them in the first place. Again, at a certain point, it usually devolves towards just keeping the train moving and hoping you can tank the enemies. Not even a skill problem, just simply not having enough damage/resources to handle them in the first place. Perfect aim, lining up explosive enemies to damage others, nothing works unless you find something broken. In other rouge-likes, you CAN beat the game off pure skill even on a terrible run. Here I feel there is no room to do so. The gameplay loop is quite fun but the difficulty and feeling of unfairness detract from that sadly. Isn't a bad game at all. Just some number adjustments could be a good change.

An outstanding roguelike that gives us a chaotic take on the roguelike genre: action combat train management. The closest comparison to Apocalypse Express would be FTL, but FTL feels positively laid back compared to this. This game does a wonderful job with all the elements that make the roguelike genre great. You've got: -Lots of transformative upgrades and sidegrades with tons of great synergies. Whenever I get to choose between 3, it's pretty rare to not have at least 1 or 2 great choices in the bunch. -Different starting trains and RNG to keep runs feeling unique. For example: on one run I was pretty much focused on plowing through each level at lightspeed and facetanking/healing through all the damage; on another, I focused on putting as many bullets downrange as possible so that they would warp around the screen, gaining damage as they warped; and on another, I was putting out tons of explosives that each had a chance of spawning more explosives. -Run-to-run upgrades that feel useful but not necessary, and they don't make things too easy or let you outlevel the challenge. -A chaotic, relatively high base difficulty that feels much more manageable once you get into the flow of combat, the components of which can vary each run depending on what types of upgrades you get. -Enemy variety that prevents one-size-fits-all solutions and keeps things interesting. Especially once you reach the second zone, you get a lot of "They can do that?!?!" moments. -A good, level-by-level save system to let you take breaks in longer runs (once you have all zones unlocked, runs can get up to 1.5 hrs) while still letting you build momentum from the different synergies in a long run. -You can optionally choose higher or lower difficulty encounters to suit your needs. -Some other mechanics are optionally enabled, so you can switch them off if you're being overloaded by everything going on onscreen. -It's being actively updated! The main potential downside is that the difficulty curve might be daunting to some if you aren't willing to take a run or several to get used to it (that said, I daresay "skill issue" to the negative reviews for that). Overall, I highly recommend this game. It's a ton of fun with high replayability, and it's a great addition to the roguelike genre.

The goal of the game is to make it through a series of train stations until you reach the final destination, all while making sure your train does not completely break down or come to a halt. Your main responsibility is keeping the train running by shoveling coal into the engine. Thankfully, coal never runs out. At the same time, you need to protect the train from various threats that appear on or alongside the tracks. While nothing immediately happens if the train stops, a relentless storm is constantly chasing you, which means standing still for too long is never an option. One of the common threats comes from raiders who attack the train with gunfire, missiles, and bombs. Their shots do not deal damage to the train's hull directly, but repeated hits will eventually cause one of the train's systems to break down and cause damage. When that happens, you need to sprint to the damaged section and repair it as quickly as possible because it becomes unusable until fixed. If the train's hull integrity drops to zero, the run is over. Progression feels very similar to a roguelite. The first sign of that is the randomly generated map, which often presents branching paths and lets you choose your next destination. Unlike many similar games where you select events, here you choose the type of reward waiting at the end of the route. The reason is simple. Most journeys involve the same core tasks, with the main differences being the difficulty level, which is clearly displayed on each destination, and occasional twists such as tougher enemy encounters in exchange for better rewards. There is a management element running beneath the action. Besides shooting raiders and shoveling coal, you must switch tracks whenever the appropriate icon appears. Missing the prompt results in a collision with a blockade. Another major responsibility involves operating a claw used to collect resources found along the railway. Since the resource icons appear well in advance, you usually have enough time to position the claw correctly before the train reaches them. Once it is lined up, the collection process is automatic, so you can return to other duties. The most important resource is ammunition for your weapons, while scrap serves as the game's primary currency. Rewards typically come in the form of upgrades for your modules, such as the claw, track switcher, or gun. Every station visit allows you to choose between two randomly generated upgrades, and if neither appeals to you, you can spend resources to reroll the options. For example, the claw can be upgraded to collect more resources, the track switcher can operate automatically, or your weapon can deal additional damage. Some upgrades come with negative effects, but these are often paired with powerful bonuses that make the tradeoff worthwhile. Upgrades are also available in several rarity tiers. Beyond the starting equipment, you can unlock additional modules such as autocannons, missile launchers, ammo factories, and several other entertaining things. Some destinations lead to shops where scrap can be spent on a larger selection of upgrades, including entirely new modules. Shops also let you restock ammunition, repair hull damage, and purchase extra wagons. Additional wagons provide valuable space for more modules, since each one requires room on the train. The final reward category consists of relics, which grant passive bonuses such as reduced fire damage or slow automatic repairs. Enemies become increasingly dangerous with every new route. Sometimes, when you are close to reaching a station, it makes more sense to focus entirely on feeding coal into the engine and ignore damaged modules. You might suffer additional damage, but reaching a station instantly destroys all enemies and repairs every broken system. The train's hull is the exception, as it can only be repaired at a shop. Although the ultimate objective is reaching the final station, doing so is surprisingly achievable on a first run. Even during chaotic moments where enemies surround the train and nearly every module is broken, survival often comes down to holding out long enough to reach the next station. The real challenge begins afterward. The boss encounter can quickly destroy your modules and leave you helpless, desperately trying to decide what to repair first before it gets blown apart again. Most of the time, you’re stuck in a cycle that doesn’t end well for you. Fortunately, every failed run contributes to permanent progression. You unlock new modules, additional upgrades for each module type, and new relics. Most content is already available from the start, while the remaining unlocks have clear requirements that are naturally completed over multiple runs rather than through tedious grinding. Defeating bosses also unlocks new train models, each featuring its own unique strengths and bonuses, and new features at the base.

It's fine. The game does have a pretty decent gameplay loop and is enganging. But it also has several notable quirks and flaws that might make it hard to enjoy. Most notably, runs are very long once you unlock the later stages. Without any real way to speed things up. And secondly, the game relies a lot on quick time events and otherwise responding quickly to stuff. If you want to know more, then here is just some various points. Good: Game does a good job at avoiding infomation overload by making several pieces of UI be unlocked rather then on by default. Bad: Game does a bad job at telling you what enemies do, whilst they are usually obvious enough to figure out, even after beating the final boss I still don't know what several enemies even do. A beastiary of sort, even if it only revealed information after X number of Kills or something, would be much appriciated. Mixed: Modules feel very diffrent, whilst falling into 2 main categories of extra guns, and utilities. However, whilst they feel diffrent, several are just way undertuned. Some guns like the autocannon and minigun eat ammo very fast whilst doing very little damage. And by the stats in-game, I think the physical plates are just broken and don't do anything at all. Bad: Ammo as a mechanic. All guns share a ammo pool, I get the point is to stop weapon spam from being a viable strat, but there is next to no infomation about how much ammo each gun is using, meaning it's easy to be good on ammo, add 1 extra weapon, and suddenly be bleeding out of ammo very fast. If you run out of ammo, like I once did vs the first boss, you just kinda have to wait for random ammo pickups on the path, and then watch it last for 5 seconds since you can't turn off weapons that aren't helping and just wasting it. Good: Upgrades generall are mostly useful, with only the rare exeption being build dependant, or just understated. BAD: Dying is very slow. your train is soo tanky, that even if all your modules are destoryed, it takes a while for enemies to kill you. The reason this is an issue is because if things go out of your control, and enemies stack up several waves, then it becomes imposible to repair stuff faster then it gets taken down again. This leads to you knowing you are dead since you can't do anything, but still have to wait for a whole minute to actually die. Repair your weapons? You can't kill enemies fast enough to get rid of them before the next wave flows in. Repair the engine to make a get away? Several enemies exist purely to stop you from doing this, and this is also imposible in boss fights. I know I am being very critical about the game here, but I still think the game is solid, I just want you to know the issues befure you go in.

Excellent game for an excellent price. It's pretty tough to get far, it has local co op, and most importantly, it's fun. You have a train that you have to load coal into, it has various compartments which you can get modules for, then you run around interacting with them trying to defend and collect resources while also keeping your train moving forward. These leads to a chaotic balance between everything. The roguelite mechanics mean you get different upgrades, modules, and relics each time. There is meta progression as well but it doesn't break the game. There are also various features that unlock as you complete the runs and unlock the new areas. Each module can be damaged and has to be repaired, there is a claw you use to pick up items, and the guns have a timer on reloading. Time management is super important and reloading before jumping off a weapon is vital. There is a lever to change tracks, when you get a warning to change tracks, if you ignore it you'll go on the wrong track and hit a destroyed train car and will blow up your engine which you'll then have to repair. Overall it's very good and what I particularly like over other games in similar genres is the time pressure. You have to constantly push forward which adds more tension and chaos. Edit:At 10 hours I've unlocked a ton of things, most of the radar upgrades, a minigame for repairing and shoveling coal that repairs and refills faster, the ability to overfill coal, 3 additional trains and 3 additional maps. I still haven't really completed a full run as each run ends on the furtherst map you've gotten to. As it is now, it seems the game requires 5 progressively longer runs to win as you have to make your way through the earlier maps to see the later ones. Once you beat the third map with a train, you unlock a special item which embodies that trains special ability. You beat the mission with the gun train and unlock a twin shot gun, and if you beat it with the interstellar train your bullets wrap around the screen. Overall this is really fun and encourages you to try all the trains out and get decently good with them. Also once the runs get longer it becomes so much more fun. You have so many train segments and so many modules it takes forever to run back and forth. Then you have the overfilling coal which makes the game like 50% faster but way more chaotic as you have less time to do everything and if you mess up, your train blows up. The game also has a lot of little things to help you manage as well. When I tried the shield train I ended up getting so many modules that I couldn't keep up with repairing everything, even with the significant damage reductions. I ended up getting an upgrade which repaired every module slowly but because of the overwhelming damage reduction I had, it basically made me immortal. Overall, I really enjoy these mechanics.

Neat little roguelite inspired by FTL, with spaces for modules, hull points, scrap, node based exploration, etc. With a few key differences: 1) One man army. You only control a single guy, no crew to manage. 2) In conjunction with that, the action is all real time (by design), so no strategic pause. 3) Mostly manual aiming/firing of weapons. These 3 elements combined make for some hectic segments, for better or worse, so if you're averse to real time decision making, then maybe pass on this one. Overall, I think the developer succeeded in making a decent clone of FTL, with a neat thematic setting (post-apocalypse) and mechanically different enough. It does not come close to matching the overall polish of FTL in all areas, but it is decent enough that it can scratch that itch for a short while.

[Literally posted said review and then they updated the game. Currently the game seems better, however, before the update, you could potentially have a good run. The problem was more those were fewer, or in the case of my example, could be going good, running hard points and in the end you instantly get wrecked by the fact you never saw any module adding spots. As I said, so far, there seemed to be more module adding areas. For now I recommended, because overall the design and game play are good and fun and the update shows they still are giving the game attention.] This game has so much potential but it is let down by balancing so bad. It is not just numbers on damage and such either. I have gone so long with no extra modules being an option on the trail. Meanwhile then you get to the boss and feel completely trashed, even though you were doing hard runs and getting legendary bonuses. My last run I had several of these. I scored on a random chance. I had other great ones like repair 25 percent next to you, extra explosion damage, several gun upgrades in terms of a reflector and firing speed. I was running hard choices the entire trail. Get to the first boss and in a couple seconds of the start, literally 3-5 seconds, six or seven drones are hitting different areas and taking no damage from the claw's auto damage field I built and hitting them with the gun is tedious at best, especially with massive reload times where you can do little else. It just did not feel good to go through so much hard only to instantly, I want to stress it was about max 5 seconds, have the entire train on fire. And again, you see the picture with many guns, yet in this hard run, I got one, one extra module choice. There were no others. That is something that is always happening as well. Add in your usual, you'll get bad choices or some that do not fit and it becomes not a hard game, but a tedious, frustrating one where you doing well does not add up, like it does in most RL builders.
